bull_bear.body: Focus on R&D (INR 750-800 cr) for complex/peptide pipeline; In-licensing deals for US branded portfolio; Disciplined working capital management; No dividend/buyback specific commentary.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: US pricing pressure persistence; Delayed FDA approvals for F2/F3 lines; Higher-than-expected burn from US branded rollout; Peptide development execution risk; Currency fluctuation (INR/USD).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasis on 'execution-led' strategy over market tailwinds; Transparent about short-term margin drag for long-term platform building; Disciplined on capital allocation.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The Q4 R&D spike (11% of sales) was an outlier due to specific peptide batch costs and will normalize to ~9%; F2/F3 facilities are already generating contract manufacturing revenue in FY27, earlier than some peers' typical ramp-up; US Branded strategy is 'calibrated entry' via in-licensing (no heavy capex) rather than organic build.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'Consistent dividend payout' is listed as an explicit element of the company's value proposition (no payout ratio or amount is given in the deck).
- ROCE shown at 14% (FY23), 15% (FY24), 16% (FY25) and 15% (FY26), excluding assets not deployed and exceptional items; FY23 is stated without the one-time Aleor write-off for comparability.
- Reinvestment is running through both capex (INR 3.45-5.75 bn a year over FY24-FY26) and a re-accelerating R&D line (7.6% of sales in FY24 to 9.6% in FY26), alongside inorganic steps (Utility Therapeutics acquisition, Canadian JV).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- R&D intensity of roughly 10% of revenue, weighted toward complex generics and peptides
- USFDA-approved Oncology and Injectables facilities positioned in complex, high-barrier manufacturing categories
- Pivya (women's health) carries an established European commercialisation history, reducing regulatory/clinical risk on U.S. entry
- Century-strong legacy with regulatory trust built market by market
- Global footprint spanning 74 countries with exports contributing 57% of turnover
- Manufacturing partnerships with large global pharmaceutical companies validating platform capability and quality
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory/quality risk at USFDA-inspected manufacturing facilities — The Injectable Formulation Facility (F-3) was inspected by the USFDA during FY26 and received 2 observations; while an EIR was subsequently received for F-3 and EIRs are now in place for all USFDA-inspected facilities, the company's regulated-market business remains exposed to ongoing inspection risk across its manufacturing network.
- Revenue concentration in International Business (exports) — The International Business (formulation and API exports) continues to contribute a significant and growing share of consolidated revenue, making performance sensitive to global pricing pressure, regulatory shifts and geopolitical dynamics in export markets.
- Execution risk on the U.S. branded-specialty pivot — Alembic's push into brand-led specialty in the U.S. (women's health, via the newly acquired Utility Therapeutics/Pivya platform) depends on a newly built commercial field force and an unproven brand-commercialisation capability for a company historically built on generics manufacturing; script/prescription uptake is not guaranteed.
- Capacity utilisation and return-on-capital risk in Oncology & Injectables facilities — Alembic describes its complex, USFDA-approved Oncology and Injectables facilities as having come through a capital-intensive investment phase and still moving toward stronger utilisation; the expected efficiency gains and overhead absorption depend on utilisation actually ramping as anticipated.
- Milestone-linked M&A consideration risk (Utility Therapeutics) — A significant portion of the Utility Therapeutics acquisition consideration is linked to future commercial milestones rather than paid upfront, so the ultimate cost and value realisation of the deal depend on the acquired business achieving those milestones.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- India branded business is ranked 21st in the Indian Pharmaceutical Market with a 1.1% market share (IQVIA MAT Jun-26); the company also ranks 17th by prescription volume with 137.6 million prescriptions (MAT Jun 2026), up from 131.3 million a year earlier, and 0.246 mn prescribers (Jun-26) versus 0.237 mn (Jun-25).
- Portfolio leadership shown brand-by-brand: 14 brands ranked No.1 or No.2 in their molecule groups, including ROXID (95.1% MS, rank 1), ALTHROCIN (87.8%, rank 1), ELATA (52.4%, rank 1), DELTONE (52.0%, rank 1), AZITHRAL (34.8%, rank 1), GERIJOINT (33.9%, rank 1) and CRINA-NCR (31.7%, rank 1); five flagship brands have surpassed INR 1 billion in sales.
- US business described as an 'established US front-end with a strong customer base', with 185 generic formulations commercialized in the USA to date and a cumulative record of 279 ANDA filings and 244 approvals (including 20 tentative).
- Animal Health is a distinct franchise: operates in Livestock, Poultry and Companion Animal segments and is described as market leader in Haematinics and Antibiotics with brands Sharkoferrol, Moxel, Xceft and Mceft.
- Company scale per 'Company at a Glance': 9 manufacturing facilities, 2 R&D centres, 208 brands, team size 17,200+, tracing back to 1907 (Amin family) with the pharmaceutical business demerged from the Alembic Group in 2010.

business.body:
- [Corporate history] Aleor Dermaceuticals (a JV formed in 2016) was merged into Alembic Pharma in 2022; Rhizen, a JV for NCE research, was formed in 2012; the pharmaceutical business itself was demerged from the Alembic Group in 2010.
- [Acquisition] Utility Therapeutics Limited was acquired in 2025, alongside commissioning of the Indore facility.
- [US branded entry] 2026 marks expansion into the US branded footprint through Alembic Therapeutics — a structural shift away from a purely generics US model, flagged in the deck as 'planned strategic expansion in US branded business'.
- [Regulatory] F3-Karkhadi received its EIR on May 13, 2026 following the Feb'26 USFDA audit, and the Indore facility received WHO certification in Apr'26.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthening growth momentum in specialty therapies in the India Branded Business (FY27 priority)
- Progressively build branded specialty presence in the U.S. (FY27 priority)
- Accelerate the launch and commercialisation of complex, differentiated generics and specialty therapies across the U.S. market (FY27 priority)
- Expanding geographical footprint across select markets in Rest of the World (FY27 priority)
- Actively pursuing in-licensing opportunities to augment the pipeline and support measured entry into specialised segments
- Calibrating R&D investment at approximately 8-9% of sales going forward, with a progressive shift toward complex generics, injectables and peptides
- Diversifying the portfolio by combining the stability of a predominantly regulated RoW business with a milestone-based approach to the U.S.-branded opportunity, to emerge as a higher-value, specialised player
- Capital allocation is described as disciplined, favouring preservation of balance-sheet strength: the Utility Therapeutics acquisition linked a significant portion of consideration to future milestones so payments largely coincide with commercial value/cash-flow creation, rather than upfront outlay. Dividend policy has been raised for FY26 to Rs.12/- per share (600%) from Rs.11/- (550%) for FY25, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, with no amount transferred to reserves during the year. Working-capital financing needs were met through a mix of bank loans and commercial paper issuance rather than long-term debt.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Alembic executed an F1-to-F4 strategic pivot at its Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) facilities: F1 (Panelav) had historically combined high-volume commercial production with new product development, creating capacity constraints. All high-volume OSD production has been transitioned to F4 (Jarod), freeing F1 to focus on exhibit batches for filings and commercial volumes of complex, high-value products; a specialised small-batch, high-value production unit is being established within F4 for new product launches and future regulatory exhibit batches. F2 (Panelav) and F3 (Karkhadi) form Alembic's oncology, injectables and ophthalmics infrastructure, currently operating below optimal utilisation, with FY26 actions targeted at improving overhead absorption and preparing for stronger utilisation. F3 runs three production lines: a Vial Line (operational, 4th line near-completion) used for own products, CMO and in-licensing; a Syringe Line (operational, pre-filled syringes/auto-injectors/pens) with GLP-1 exhibit batches planned to raise utilisation in FY27; and an Ophthalmic Line operating near-full capacity, with an additional high-speed ophthalmic filling line targeted for operational status by end of FY27 to meet demand. A specialised microspheres line is in advanced development for future specialty product contributions. F2 is pursuing selective Contract Manufacturing Organisation (CMO) opportunities and out-licensing (e.g. liposomal doxorubicin, docetaxel approved and out-licensed to large pharmaceutical partners). During FY26, Alembic also commissioned a new facility at Pithampur (April 2025) - centrally located in India for materially better distribution reach, with modern production infrastructure and substantially expanded capacity for domestic branded formulations, with volumes migrating there through a transition period. An API III facility, dedicated to internal API needs and external sales, was also commissioned in April 2025. A dedicated F5 facility handles various dermatology dosage forms.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global pharmaceutical demand is underpinned by rising chronic disease burden, an ageing population and adoption of high-value therapies (oncology, GLP-1/obesity, immunology), which together account for a disproportionate share of incremental growth
- Patent expiries and biosimilar/generic competition are expanding access and creating opportunities for generics and niche complex products, particularly in the U.S. market
- India Branded Business and RoW portfolio provide a stable, less-commoditised revenue base, while the U.S. branded-specialty opportunity is being pursued via a milestone-based approach
- API business growth is driven by cost optimisation (solvent recovery, process improvements, debottlenecking, enhanced asset utilisation) and deepening backward integration/captive consumption
- A resilient supply chain, strong regulatory compliance track record and scalable operations support timely, focused execution amid an environment of supply disruptions
- Competitive intensity is rising even within higher-barrier categories, and large outsized R&D opportunities are more limited than in earlier cycles, reinforcing the need for disciplined portfolio selection
- 94 products filed across multiple RoW markets (Thailand, South Africa, Singapore, Latin America, Iraq, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, Hong Kong) during FY26, underpinning a launch pipeline with commercialisation planned from FY27 onwards
- 10 ANDAs filed during FY26 (complex products, injectables, peptides, select first-to-file/NCE-1 opportunities); 22 ANDA approvals received during the year, including tentative approvals
- Development portfolio now includes a balanced mix of first-to-file opportunities, oncology products and non-oral solid-dosage platforms
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Alembic Pharma delivered resilient Q4FY26 growth (4% YoY revenue) driven by US volume launches and India specialty brands, though margins faced a ~100-150 bps drag from the new US branded 'Pivya' launch and elevated peptide R&D. The strategic pivot toward high-value US branded assets and complex peptides positions FY27 for low double-digit top-line growth, with margin recovery expected as operating leverage from core generics offsets initial branded start-up costs.
